label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To: posts/new
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Correction: the GST formula in my takings template was wrong

The daily takings and GST template I posted on 12 August had a wrong GST formula. If you used v1.0, v1.1 or v1.2 and keyed in GST-inclusive takings, the sheet showed more GST than you actually collected. I fixed this in v1.3, uploaded on 8 November, and the download link on the original post now gives you that version.

What was wrong

Column F took your daily takings and multiplied them by 9%. That is only right if the takings exclude GST. Most stall owners key in what went into the till, which already includes GST. For those figures the GST portion is 9/109 of the amount, not 9%.

Ravi's figures show it clearly. His takings for one day were $1,090, GST inclusive. The template gave GST of $98.10. The correct figure is $90. The sheet overstated his GST by $8.10 for that day, and it did the same on every row.

Who is affected

Anyone who entered GST-inclusive amounts into v1.0 (12 Aug), v1.1 (2 Sep) or v1.2 (1 Oct). The template has been downloaded 412 times since 12 August, so this is not a small group. If the amounts you entered excluded GST, the old formula gave you the right answer.

Two things to keep in mind. The error overstates GST, so nobody has underpaid IRAS because of it. And the quarterly sales total for Box 1 is worked out separately and was correct in every version. Only the Box 6 figure was affected.

How I missed it

I tested v1.0 against my own sample figures, and those figures were already ex-GST. The check passed, and I never tested the sheet the way most of you would use it. The mistake was mine. Melvin said in the comments that people trust this kind of thing because I say I am an accountant. He is right, and that is exactly why I should have tested it properly. I am sorry.

Thank you Ravi for spotting it and asking, and Shu Fen for pinning down the formula and telling me to put up a proper correction.

If you already filed your July to September return with the old sheet

1. Download v1.3 from the original post.
2. Check cell H2. Set it to match the amounts you key in, not your menu. Choose 'prices exclude GST' only if the amounts you enter exclude GST. If you enter receipts that include the GST collected, use the inclusive setting, even if your menu prices are shown before GST.
3. Copy your daily takings for the quarter into v1.3 and compare the new Box 6 figure with the one you filed. The difference is what you may have overpaid.
4. Do not simply adjust your next return on your own. IRAS has its own rules on whether an error can go into a later GST F5 or needs a GST F7. Look up the page on correcting errors in GST returns on the IRAS website, or ask whoever files for you, and follow that route.
5. Keep both the old sheet and the new one, so you can show how the difference came about.

I cannot amend anyone's return for them. The correction has to come from you or your filer. But if anything in v1.3 is unclear, leave a comment and I will answer.

If you have not filed yet

Move your figures to v1.3 before you do, and check H2 first.

In my earlier comment I asked you to hold off changing your records until I had confirmed what went wrong. You can go ahead now.
